subject: Urgent: Request for data extraction authority and evidence transfer from FinLane incident
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara@finlane.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs

Vanessa,

We detected anomalous outbound transfers from our integration with Redwood last night (June 29). We need Redwood to provide: (1) a forensic export of the claimant customer records (customer IDs provided in the attached manifest), (2) request/response logs for the time window 2026-06-29 22:00 - 2026-06-30 02:00 UTC, and (3) subprocessor access logs for any third-party services involved.

FinLane legal would prefer a direct export to our forensics partner (forensica.io) to avoid extended e-discovery timelines. Please confirm scope and whether Redwood requires an authorization document signed by FinLane before transferring exports out of Redwood-managed storage.

Attachments: finlane_manifest_20260630.csv

Thanks,
Sara Park
Head of Security Operations
FinLane
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@finlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs

Sara —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the manifest. We're treating this as high priority. Initial answers up front: yes, we can produce the requested exports and logs, but we need: (a) a signed limited-purpose authorization (we typically call this a Forensic Evidence Transfer Addendum), and (b) clarity on whether FinLane authorizes delivery to a third-party forensics vendor listed in the manifest (forensica.io).

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I will kick off triage with infra (Ben) and Legal (Kimberly) now.
- We aim to provide an initial telemetry snapshot and a containment note within 4 hours.
- If you can confirm authorization to deliver to forensica.io, include the contact (name + email) and preferred transfer method (S3 presigned, encrypted scp, or managed transfer portal).

We will also document the subprocessor chain and provide a log export. If the export contains cross-border data, Legal will need to check transfers and any DPA constraints (we will flag any carve-outs).

—Vanessa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs

Vanessa / Kim —

I've started a containment snapshot on the clusters that handled FinLane traffic. Engineering notes: we can generate the requested request/response logs and a db export slice limited to IDs in the manifest. Export methods we support:
- S3 presigned (bucket redwood-incident-exports, TTL 24h)
- PGP-encrypted tarball (delivered over managed transfer)
- Direct push to a customer-managed S3 if FinLane provides a write-capable role

Subprocessor logs: we'll pull access logs from any managed ingress points (auth provider, observability pipeline). That may include data from our CDN partner and the telemetry pipeline (two subprocessors).

Two operational clarifications before export: 1) do we sanitize tokens/keys from the exported logs? 2) is FinLane comfortable with an export that contains subprocessor identifiers (we can mask them if required).

I'll also produce an export manifest template (attaching).

Attachments: s3_export_manifest_template.csv

—Ben
Head of Infra Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Park <sara@finlane.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs

All —

From a legal / DPA perspective:
- Our standard practice is to require a Forensic Evidence Transfer Addendum (FETA) executed by the customer that narrowly scopes data use to investigation and prohibits further retention or re-sharing. This addresses DPA obligations and subprocessor export constraints.
- If the export would cause personal data to cross jurisdictions (e.g., EU -> US), we need to confirm lawful transfer basis or use encrypted transfer with customer-controlled keys.
- For subprocessor logs: confirm whether FinLane's DPA with its own downstream vendors imposes any constraints; we will redact or pseudonymize subprocessor identifiers on request.

Recommended immediate actions:
1) FinLane signs a short FETA (I can send a redline of the template today).
2) FinLane confirms acceptance of either S3 presigned (preferred for auditability) or PGP envelope.
3) If FinLane wants direct delivery to forensica.io, we need a named contact and a binding transfer acceptance email copy from FinLane legal.

I'll draft a one-page FETA and attach the draft concurrently.

—Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Park <sara@finlane.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs

Thanks, team. FinLane confirms:
- We authorize transfer to Forensica (lead: Mark Li, mark.li@forensica.io).
- Preferred transfer: S3 presigned links (24h TTL) to FinLane-managed bucket; if not possible, PGP-encrypted tar delivered via secure portal.
- FinLane legal will sign the FETA; please send the draft.

Additional asks: can Redwood provide a short list of subprocessors that touched the records (names + region) and whether any subprocessors are outside the EU for the dataset (we have EU-resident customers in the manifest). We need that detail to satisfy internal regulatory reporting.

Attachment: confirmation_email_finlane_20260701.txt

—Sara
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@finlane.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible exfil — request for data export and logs — agreed approach and timeline

Sara —

Thanks for confirming. Summary of agreed approach and timeline (so everyone has a single source of truth):
1) Authorization: Kimberly will circulate the FETA draft by EOD 2026-07-02; FinLane legal to countersign (we expect execution within 48 hours).
2) Containment snapshot: Ben has completed a live snapshot; initial telemetry summary sent to FinLane via secure channel within 4 hours of the original notice.
3) Subprocessor list: We will provide a redacted list (names + regions) by 2026-07-03 12:00 PDT. Any subprocessor PII exposure flags will be highlighted.
4) Export method: Primary option — S3 presigned links to FinLane-managed bucket. If FinLane cannot accept writes, we'll provide a PGP-encrypted tar delivered via our managed portal. Presigned links will be TTL 24 hours and logged.
5) Evidence transfer: Once FETA is executed, Redwood will produce the export and provide presigned link(s) within 7 calendar days. If emergency expedited transfer is required, we can accelerate to 48-72 hours but this requires an exception approval from Ops and Legal (documented).
6) Chain of custody: Forensica will be copied on the transfer confirmation and provided with the S3 manifest and MD5 checksums.
7) Cross-border: If export includes EU-origin data, we'll apply customer-controlled encryption keys or mask identifiers until legal sign-off.

Attachments included here: redwood_forensic_addendum_v1.pdf (draft FETA), s3_export_manifest_template.csv

If that aligns, please reply with any objections; otherwise we'll proceed with drafting and the export plan.

—Vanessa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
